assessment.nobel_worthiness: Turns a biological process, ubiquitin-dependent proteolysis, into a designable chemical reaction: bifunctional degraders and molecular glues (thalidomide analogues acting through cereblon) hijack an E3 ligase to destroy a chosen protein. Original, mechanistically well defined, a general tool for biologists and already producing clinical drugs against targets once considered undruggable.
assessment.attribution: Crews and colleagues conceived and demonstrated PROTACs; Deshaies helped build the field and early degrader technology; Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target, which explains molecular glues. Ciulli, Sakamoto, Kim, Gray, Ito are also credible, so a three-person cap forces hard trade-offs between the PROTAC and molecular-glue arms.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced by many groups and in clinical trials; the field is mature enough for recognition, although approved degrader drugs are still few and the long-term clinical record is short.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should span PROTACs and molecular glues or only one arm
Who is decisive among Ciulli, Sakamoto, Kim, Gray and Ito
Clinical impact is still emerging

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors are a chemical solution to genome editing: engineered deaminases fused to a Cas protein convert C to T or A to G without double-strand breaks. Highly original, mechanistically clear and directly relevant to genome maintenance and to correcting disease mutations, with first clinical uses.
assessment.attribution: Liu is the clear senior leader; Komor and Gaudelli, as the lead trainees, made the cytosine and adenine base editors. Kondo and Nishida independently reported a deaminase-based editor, so credit is not entirely unambiguous. A prize might be Liu alone or with the CRISPR-related lineage already recognised in 2020.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed across organisms and in therapeutic settings; the foundations are about a decade old and well reproduced. Slightly early for clinical verdict, but scientific timing is good.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2020 CRISPR prize may weigh on the committee
Priority question between Liu and the Kondo/Nishida work
Off-target deamination and long-term safety are not fully resolved

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantitative, large-scale mass spectrometric proteomics made it possible to measure thousands of proteins and modifications in cells, which is the biochemical measurement base for questions like nucleotide metabolism and its regulation. Lasting impact is enormous and broad across biology and medicine.
assessment.attribution: Mann (high-resolution MS-based proteomics and SILAC-style quantification), Aebersold (targeted and SRM/SWATH-like approaches, ICAT) and Yates (shotgun/MudPIT, database search) are the major distinct methodological pillars. Hunt, Gygi and Heck are also strong, so any three exclude important contributors. The ionisation methods were recognised in 2002.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature, validated for two decades and universal in practice. Recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2002 prize for ionisation and MS of macromolecules
Selecting three from a six-person field
Whether the committee sees this as a tool and not a discovery

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reversible methylation of RNA and the writer, eraser and reader system revealed a new chemical layer of gene regulation, in analogy to DNA and histone epigenetics. Conceptually original with broad biological and disease relevance, and the underlying chemistry (methyl transferase and demethylase mechanisms) is well defined.
assessment.attribution: He proposed reversible RNA methylation and identified FTO as an m6A demethylase; Jaffrey and Rechavi (with Dominissini and Meyer) mapped m6A transcriptome-wide, which launched the field. Jia, Yang and others share early credit. Fair allocation is tricky across the discovery and the mapping.
assessment.maturity: Broadly reproduced, though debates continue about the specificity of mapping methods, antibody artefacts and the physiological role of some readers and erasers (including FTO substrates). Reasonably mature, still evolving.
uncertainties: Controversy over m6A mapping specificity and FTO substrate preference
Allocation among He, Jaffrey, Rechavi and the Jia/Yang group
Whether chemistry or physiology is the dominant contribution

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing by synthesis, built on reversible-terminator nucleotide chemistry and polymerase engineering, transformed biology and medicine. As a person who works with polymerases and nucleotides I regard the chemistry of reversible terminators as the decisive invention.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman founded Solexa chemistry and sequencing by synthesis; Mayer is credited for clustered/colony amplification; Rothberg for pyrosequencing-based parallel sequencing; Ju for terminator chemistry. Overlapping commercial and patent claims make credit contested.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature with immense impact; the Sanger-era prize was in 1980 and recognition of this one is plausible.
uncertainties: Credit split between sequencing-by-synthesis and pyrosequencing lineages
Commercial and priority disputes
Possible perception of a technology and not a chemical discovery

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Orthogonal aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase/tRNA pairs allow site-specific incorporation of noncanonical amino acids into proteins in living cells, reprogramming the genetic code. A general chemical tool that made new covalent chemistry available to biologists, and it is widely used.
assessment.attribution: Schultz established the first orthogonal pairs and the field; Wang, then in Schultz's group, made key early advances; Chin extended it to higher organisms and to quadruplet codons and ribosome engineering. Mehl and Yokoyama are also credible.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed in many laboratories and commercial uses; the area is mature, though therapeutic applications remain early.
uncertainties: Dividing credit between Schultz and later developers like Chin
Therapeutic or practical impact versus tool status
Overlap with the 2018 directed evolution and 2018 phage display recognition is minor but worth a check

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Activity-based protein profiling uses mechanism-based covalent probes to read out enzyme function directly in complex proteomes, turning enzymology into a proteome-wide chemical measurement. It fits my preference for measurement of activity over abundance and produced both new drug targets and inhibitors.
assessment.attribution: Cravatt developed and generalised ABPP; Bogyo and Overkleeft contributed probe design for protease and proteasome classes; Weerapana contributed isoTOP-ABPP cysteine profiling. Cravatt appears the most decisive.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed and widely adopted; clinical compounds derived from covalent chemoproteomics are emerging, which supports timeliness.
uncertainties: Whether Cravatt alone or a set of three best reflects the contribution
Relative novelty compared with earlier mechanism-based inhibitor work
Impact is broad but diffuse across applications

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles enable delivery of siRNA and mRNA and underpinned the mRNA vaccines and the first siRNA drug. Impact on public health is extraordinary, and the underlying lipid chemistry, pKa-tuned ionisable lipids, is a real chemical design principle.
assessment.attribution: Cullis's group developed the formation and ionizable-lipid delivery principles; Hope and Madden were core coauthors; Anderson and Langer contributed lipidoid and polymer delivery; MacLachlan contributed in industry. The 2023 Medicine prize recognised the mRNA modification science, not the delivery chemistry.
assessment.maturity: Validated at global scale through vaccines and approved siRNA therapy; recognition is mature, though the credit landscape is crowded.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2023 Medicine prize
Credit spread across academic, industrial and polymer-delivery contributors
Whether this belongs to chemistry or to pharmaceutical sciences
